title: The 10 Best Tap and Die Sets
subtitle: SAE and metric tap and die sets for cutting and repairing threads, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A tap and die set cuts new threads and cleans up damaged ones on bolts and holes. We ranked 10 best-sellers from GEARWRENCH, OMT, EFFICERE and value brands on rating, review volume and features (metric and SAE sizes, ratcheting handles, a thread pitch gauge and sizes past 1/2 inch).

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

avoid.name: KJE 86-Piece SAE and Metric Tap and Die Set, #4 to 5/8 in and M3 to M16
avoid.flag: Contradicts itself on what steel it's made of
avoid.verdict: A titanium-coated set that claims high-speed steel in its bullets while its spec table also lists bearing steel, with the lowest rating of the sets we looked at.
reasons: The bullets say the taps and dies are 'high-speed steel with titanium plating', but the material field lists 'GCr15 Bearing Steel, High-speed steel, Titanium'. HSS and GCr15 are different steels, so it's unclear which you get.
It claims '3x longer service life' from the coating without saying compared to what.
It's rated 4.0 stars. The OMT 80-piece costs less, has 2,197 reviews and says plainly that it's bearing steel.

buyers_guide.q: What's the difference between a tap and a die?
buyers_guide.a: A tap cuts internal threads in a hole. A die cuts external threads on a rod or bolt. Most repair work is chasing damaged threads rather than cutting new ones.
A taper tap starts threads easily. A plug tap goes deeper. A bottoming tap finishes threads to the bottom of a blind hole. Sets with both taper and plug taps handle more jobs.
Most affordable sets use GCr15 bearing steel, fine for chasing threads and soft metals. High-speed steel lasts longer and cuts hard steel and stainless better.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a pitch gauge?
buyers_guide.a: Yes, if you don't know the thread. A pitch gauge tells you threads per inch or millimeter pitch so you pick the right tap.
Drill the correct tap-drill size, use cutting oil, and back the tap off a half turn every turn or two to break chips.
